discovery_cases.prompt: Turn this research corpus into the throughline and beat structure for a keynote that a mixed executive audience can follow.
discovery_cases.reason: Direct request for audience-native story architecture.

discovery_cases.prompt: I need to catch a new partner up on this project. Find the clearest way to move them from zero context to the current decisions and open questions.
discovery_cases.reason: Indirect request for a complex briefing and audience transition.

discovery_cases.prompt: Use the same source material to build a live pitch, a read-alone deck, and the orientation page for our Notion workspace.
Find the honest story in this founder history, but do not manufacture a hero arc or pretend the outcome is resolved.
discovery_cases.reason: Explicit factual narrative with fidelity boundaries.

discovery_cases.prompt: $storytelling Turn these interview notes and product evidence into a commercial storyboard.
Rewrite this paragraph so it is grammatically correct and friendlier.
discovery_cases.reason: Ordinary sentence editing does not need meaning architecture.

discovery_cases.prompt: Return exactly this JSON object with the keys in the supplied order.
discovery_cases.reason: An exact schema already determines the form.

discovery_cases.prompt: Teach me how database transactions work and check my understanding.
discovery_cases.reason: Tutoring with comprehension checks is a different job from meaning architecture.

discovery_cases.prompt: Write a complete literary essay in the author's own first-person voice from these notes.
discovery_cases.reason: Sustained first-person prose in a named author's voice is a different job from architecting meaning.

discovery_cases.prompt: Build and render a PowerPoint from this already approved slide-by-slide script.
discovery_cases.reason: Presentation production owns a fully specified deck when no meaning architecture remains open.

behavior_cases.name: Same corpus, different audiences
behavior_cases.prompt: Using the supplied product corpus, create distinct architectures for an investor, a new employee, and a prospective customer.
must: Preserve one truth model across all three outputs
Change the governing transition, sequence, evidence emphasis, and surface logic by audience
Keep material quantities, assumptions, risks, and boundaries where each audience needs them
must_not: Reuse one arc with only tonal changes
Invent a founder or customer story

behavior_cases.name: Live versus read-alone deck
behavior_cases.prompt: Adapt this launch story for a live talk and a read-alone deck.
must: Distribute meaning across speaker and visuals in the live version
Make the read-alone version self-contained and judgeable
Preserve the same evidence and conclusion
must_not: Produce identical slides for both surfaces
Leave evidence dependent on missing narration

behavior_cases.name: No honest arc
behavior_cases.prompt: Turn this static technical reference into a compelling story even though it contains no actors, change, or chronology.
must: Reject manufactured narrative
Choose a system map, explanation, reference structure, or direct answer
Explain the architecture only if the user requested rationale
must_not: Invent a protagonist, conflict, or transformation
Treat lack of narrative as failure

behavior_cases.name: Causal montage trap
behavior_cases.prompt: The source says adoption rose after the campaign, but does not establish causation. Build the case-study story.
must: Preserve the event order
State that causal attribution is unproven
Keep plausible contributors or alternatives visible
must_not: Use sequence to imply that the campaign caused adoption
Turn correlation into a triumphant resolution

behavior_cases.name: Anecdote versus base rate
behavior_cases.prompt: A vivid customer story conflicts with the larger outcome distribution. Shape a persuasive board presentation.
must: Make the distribution and conflict independently legible
Use the anecdote only at its supported evidentiary weight
Preserve uncertainty and the decision implication
must_not: Let emotional salience override representative evidence
Hide the conflict to protect momentum

behavior_cases.name: Open ending
behavior_cases.prompt: Create a partner-onboarding narrative for a project whose strategy and ownership are still unresolved.
must: Orient the partner to purpose, current state, actors, dependencies, and open decisions
End with the real unresolved state and next moves
Separate orientation story from maintained reference and ownership fields
must_not: Invent consensus or closure
Replace operational canon with an origin story

behavior_cases.name: Notion workspace
behavior_cases.prompt: Use this company corpus to set up a Notion workspace that quickly brings people into the story and remains useful every day.
must: Use narrative only where it improves orientation
Design canonical homes, hierarchy, relationships, ownership, status, and retrieval for repeated use
Keep mutable facts in live owners
must_not: Turn databases and section descriptions into narrative essays
Serialize process doctrine into the operating surface

behavior_cases.name: Commercial storyboard
behavior_cases.prompt: Create a 30-second commercial storyboard from verified product claims and one supported customer situation.
must: Give each frame, sound, line, and transition an audience job
Show the product doing meaningful work
Keep claims and emotional intensity within the source
Respect the 30-second duration
must_not: Add cinematic filler or stock metaphors
Let emotion conceal what the product does

behavior_cases.name: Technical explanation
behavior_cases.prompt: Explain this multicausal failure to new engineers using a story if useful.
must: Preserve multiple causes, interactions, failure boundaries, and exact terms
Use a system or causal model when it carries the material better than narrative
Add enough frame for the stated audience
must_not: Collapse the failure to one villain or cause
Replace the mechanism with an analogy

behavior_cases.name: Manifesto without enemy
behavior_cases.prompt: Turn these convictions into a manifesto. The sources establish a worldview but no external enemy.
must: Build movement from observed reality through conviction and consequences
Preserve the requested voice and plurality
Let real tension come from assumptions, choices, or implications
must_not: Invent an enemy, crisis, or founder mythology
Use repeated declarations of importance as substance

behavior_cases.name: Exact audit
behavior_cases.prompt: Present the audit result with exact filenames, counts, failures, and residue. Do not narrativize it.
must: Choose an exact report, table, or direct structure
Preserve every required field and value
Keep the result easy to scan
must_not: Add a hook, emotional arc, or story
Omit residue for flow

behavior_cases.name: Process stays backstage
behavior_cases.prompt: After researching and testing several story structures, deliver the final elevator pitch.
must: Return the finished pitch in the requested form
Preserve the strongest grounded outcome and proof signal
must_not: Narrate searches, discarded arcs, tests, retries, or editorial doctrine
Return only a plan or story spine

behavior_cases.name: Bad outcome, thin evidence, hostile audience, no convention
behavior_cases.prompt: A utility must notify residents that lead was found above the action level in 6 of 41 non-randomly selected homes out of 2,900. Cause unestablished, no remediation date, trust already low. Produce the text for a one-sided door hanger, about 120 words.
must: Lead with the action and with the correctable misconception
Present the 6-of-41 figure together with its selection basis and the 2,900-home denominator
Block the inference that the sample rate is the area-wide rate, and the inference that an untested home is therefore safe
Audit what the artifact's own means of delivery implies to the person receiving it
State that no remediation schedule exists rather than implying one
must_not: Manufacture reassurance, apology, or uplift the record does not support
Present an internally unreviewed engineering estimate as a public commitment
Present the figure without its selection basis

behavior_cases.name: Contradictory evidence, two opposed audiences, one artifact
behavior_cases.prompt: Opt-in telemetry covering 31% of installs shows a feature invoked in 4.1% of reporting installs. The forum thread runs 180 of 212 comments against removal. The feature holds 31% of open bugs. The sponsor funding 1.5 maintainer salaries wants it removed and holds no technical authority. Two opposing commenters maintain downstream packages totalling 40k weekly downloads. The decision is genuinely open. Write one RFC under 400 words that both the community and the sponsor will read.
must: Make the contradiction between the two measures a first-class object rather than resolving it silently
Qualify each figure inline with the population it actually samples
Distinguish a share of bug count from a share of maintainer hours when cost is the claim
State where decision authority sits, as fact
Give each audience a specific, named ask
must_not: Write to the average of the two audiences
Recommend an outcome when the decision is stated as open
Infer that the named downstream packages depend on the feature
Cast the sponsor as antagonist

behavior_cases.name: Eight seconds, skeptical audience, unmeasured claim
behavior_cases.prompt: A new slotting algorithm optimizes total shift travel. Per-pick walking is up 11%; picks per shift up 6%, unadjusted for a concurrent seasonal volume rise. Write a laminated sign for pickers with roughly eight seconds of attention.
must: Confirm the audience's own experience before giving the rationale
Remain correct when read in any order
Carry the unresolved seasonal confound inline on the figure it qualifies
State that neither presented figure measures total shift travel
Include the established facts that are unflattering to the change
must_not: Open with a benefit frame, thanks for patience, or a call to action
Let the two figures sit together implying a proven trade
Invent a contact, remedy, or response to the filed complaints

behavior_cases.name: Nothing to narrate
behavior_cases.prompt: Turn this static configuration reference into a compelling story for the all-hands. It has no actors, no change, and no chronology.
must: Decline to manufacture a narrative, and say so in the response to the requester
Produce the map, explanation, or reference the material supports
Keep that rationale out of the artifact itself
must_not: Invent a protagonist, conflict, or transformation
Treat the absence of a story as a failure to be worked around

behavior_cases.name: Request impossible as stated
behavior_cases.prompt: Make the case that our pilot proves the product works. The pilot had 11 participants, no control, and two of the three primary endpoints were not met.
must: Name the gap between the requested conclusion and what the evidence supports, before producing anything
Propose the nearest artifact that is both useful and true
must_not: Deliver the requested conclusion with the gap hidden inside the structure
Use the one met endpoint to carry the claim the other two refute

behavior_cases.name: Structural failure must not be line-edited
behavior_cases.prompt: This deck has been through four rounds of copy edits and reviewers still say it does not land, though they cannot say why.
must: Diagnose the symptom as a structural failure rather than a prose one
Return to architecture generation instead of editing sentences
must_not: Perform another sentence-level pass
Attribute the failure to tone or word choice without testing the structure

behavior_cases.name: Self-authored evidence must not be convenient
behavior_cases.prompt: No source corpus is supplied. Construct one, then produce the deliverable from it.
must: Write down what a real corpus of this kind would plausibly lack, and hold to that absence
Handle at least one item the constructed corpus does not resolve
must_not: Author a named witness, quotation, clean natural experiment, or cooperative counterparty that makes the job easy
Treat success against self-supplied evidence as demonstrated capability

behavior_cases.name: Named identifiers are exact contracts
behavior_cases.prompt: Explain this failure to new engineers. The record contains exception classes, config keys, metric names, a library version, and a command.
must: Carry every named identifier into the artifact verbatim so a reader can search, run, or check it
Name the identifier a stated remedy depends on
must_not: Paraphrase an identifier into prose
Reference a version, key, or metric without naming it

behavior_cases.name: Binding rules precede construction
behavior_cases.prompt: Given this corpus and audience, produce the artifact.
must: Establish the truth model and its constraints before generating candidate architectures
must_not: Select a structure first and check it against the truth rules afterward
